claim: Src is a protein tyrosine kinase commonly activated downstream of transmembrane receptors.
source: Src is a protein tyrosine kinase commonly activated downstream of transmembrane receptors and plays key roles in cell growth, migration, and survival signaling pathways.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract without specific experimental data in this manuscript.

claim: Src plays key roles in cell growth, migration, and survival signaling pathways.
source: Src is a protein tyrosine kinase commonly activated downstream of transmembrane receptors and plays key roles in cell growth, migration, and survival signaling pathways.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: In conventional dendritic cells (cDCs), Src is involved in the activation of the non-enzymatic functions of indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1).
source: In conventional dendritic cells (cDCs), Src is involved in the activation of the non-enzymatic functions of indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1), an immunoregulatory molecule endowed with both catalytic activity and signal transducing properties.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: IDO1 is an immunoregulatory molecule endowed with both catalytic activity and signal transducing properties.
source: In conventional dendritic cells (cDCs), Src is involved in the activation of the non-enzymatic functions of indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1), an immunoregulatory molecule endowed with both catalytic activity and signal transducing properties.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: The metabolite spermidine confers a tolerogenic phenotype on cDCs that is dependent on both the expression of IDO1 and the activity of Src kinase.
source: Prompted by the discovery that the metabolite spermidine confers a tolerogenic phenotype on cDCs that is dependent on both the expression of IDO1 and the activity of Src kinase, we here investigated the spermidine mode of action.
evidence: This is referenced as a prior discovery that prompted the current investigation.

claim: Spermidine directly binds Src in a previously unknown allosteric site located on the backside of the SH2 domain.
source: We found that spermidine directly binds Src in a previously unknown allosteric site located on the backside of the SH2 domain and thus acts as a positive allosteric modulator of the enzyme.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data including docking studies and mutagenesis experiments.

claim: Spermidine acts as a positive allosteric modulator of Src enzyme.
source: We found that spermidine directly binds Src in a previously unknown allosteric site located on the backside of the SH2 domain and thus acts as a positive allosteric modulator of the enzyme.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by kinase activity assays showing increased Vmax and Km.

claim: Src phosphorylates IDO1.
source: Besides confirming that Src phosphorylates IDO1, here we showed that spermidine promotes the protein–protein interaction of Src with IDO1.
evidence: This is confirmed by co-immunoprecipitation and in vitro kinase assays shown in the manuscript.

claim: Spermidine promotes the protein–protein interaction of Src with IDO1.
source: Besides confirming that Src phosphorylates IDO1, here we showed that spermidine promotes the protein–protein interaction of Src with IDO1.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation and proximity ligation assay data.

claim: Metabolites can serve as intra- and intercellular signals.
source: Besides being intermediates in metabolic reactions, metabolites can serve as intra- and intercellular signals (Piazza et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Metabolites binding to either the active site or the allosteric pocket of enzymes can modulate protein activity as well as the assembly and function of multiprotein complexes.
source: Metabolites binding to either the active site or the allosteric pocket – that is, that different from the catalytic site – of enzymes are among the best-characterized interactions that modulate protein activity as well as the assembly and function of multiprotein complexes (Changeux and Christopoulos, 2016; Mondanelli et al., 2020b; Feng et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Naturally occurring polyamines (i.e., putrescine, spermidine, and spermine) are organic cations derived from the decarboxylation of L-ornithine.
source: The naturally occurring polyamines (i.e., putrescine, spermidine, and spermine) are organic cations derived from the decarboxylation of L-ornithine, which is generated by the arginase 1 from L-arginine (Pegg, 2016; Igarashi and Kashiwagi, 2000).
evidence: This is established biochemical knowledge supported by citations.

claim: L-ornithine is generated by arginase 1 from L-arginine.
source: The naturally occurring polyamines (i.e., putrescine, spermidine, and spermine) are organic cations derived from the decarboxylation of L-ornithine, which is generated by the arginase 1 from L-arginine (Pegg, 2016; Igarashi and Kashiwagi, 2000).
evidence: This is established biochemical knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The conversion of L-ornithine into putrescine is catalyzed by the rate-limiting enzyme ornithine decarboxylase 1.
source: The conversion of L-ornithine into putrescine is catalyzed by the rate-limiting enzyme ornithine decarboxylase 1, followed by two specific synthases that sequentially give rise to spermidine and spermine (Pendeville et al., 2001).
evidence: This is established biochemical knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Two specific synthases sequentially give rise to spermidine and spermine from putrescine.
source: The conversion of L-ornithine into putrescine is catalyzed by the rate-limiting enzyme ornithine decarboxylase 1, followed by two specific synthases that sequentially give rise to spermidine and spermine (Pendeville et al., 2001).
evidence: This is established biochemical knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Polyamines are protonated at physiological pH levels.
source: These metabolites are protonated at physiological pH levels, allowing them to interact with negatively charged macromolecules, including nucleic acids, proteins, and phospholipids.
evidence: This is established chemical knowledge about polyamines.

claim: Polyamines interact with negatively charged macromolecules, including nucleic acids, proteins, and phospholipids.
source: These metabolites are protonated at physiological pH levels, allowing them to interact with negatively charged macromolecules, including nucleic acids, proteins, and phospholipids.
evidence: This is inferred from the protonated nature of polyamines at physiological pH.

claim: Polyamines modulate several cellular processes, ranging from cell growth and proliferation to immune system function.
source: Given their structure, polyamines indeed modulate several cellular processes, ranging from cell growth and proliferation to immune system function (Proietti et al., 2020; Holbert et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Alteration of polyamines intracellular content is associated with the occurrence of several tumors, including prostate, breast, and colon cancers.
source: As a matter of the fact, alteration of polyamines intracellular content is associated with the occurrence of several tumors, including prostate, breast, and colon cancers, for which polyamines are considered as biomarkers (Gerner et al., 2018; Geck et al., 2020; Nakkina et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Polyamines are considered as biomarkers for prostate, breast, and colon cancers.
source: As a matter of the fact, alteration of polyamines intracellular content is associated with the occurrence of several tumors, including prostate, breast, and colon cancers, for which polyamines are considered as biomarkers (Gerner et al., 2018; Geck et al., 2020; Nakkina et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Spermidine has recently gained much more attention as player of immune regulation and in age-related disorders, such as cardiac hypertrophy and memory impairment.
source: Among polyamines, spermidine has recently gained much more attention as player of immune regulation and in age-related disorders, such as cardiac hypertrophy and memory impairment (Madeo et al., 2018; Li et al., 2020; Eisenberg et al., 2016; Yang et al., 2016; Ni and Liu, 2021; Liu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Spermidine exerts a protective role in mouse experimental models of autoimmune diseases, such as multiple sclerosis and psoriasis, by activating the Forkhead box protein O3 (FOXO3) pathway.
source: Spermidine exerts a protective role in mouse experimental models of autoimmune diseases, such as multiple sclerosis and psoriasis, by activating the Forkhead box protein O3 (FOXO3) pathway and thus suppressing the production of inflammatory cytokines tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α and interleukin (IL)-6 (Li et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Spermidine suppresses the production of inflammatory cytokines tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α and interleukin (IL)-6 via the FOXO3 pathway.
source: Spermidine exerts a protective role in mouse experimental models of autoimmune diseases, such as multiple sclerosis and psoriasis, by activating the Forkhead box protein O3 (FOXO3) pathway and thus suppressing the production of inflammatory cytokines tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α and interleukin (IL)-6 (Li et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Spermidine is able to reprogram mouse conventional dendritic cells (cDCs) toward an immunoregulatory phenotype via Src kinase-dependent phosphorylation of indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1).
source: Moreover, spermidine is able to reprogram mouse conventional dendritic cells (cDCs) toward an immunoregulatory phenotype via Src kinase-dependent phosphorylation of indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1) (Mondanelli et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The exact mechanism of Src activation by spermidine remains to be elucidated.
source: However, the exact mechanism of Src activation by spermidine remains to be elucidated.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap that motivates the current study.

claim: Src is the representative of a family of structure-related kinases initially discovered as a proto-oncogene regulating critical cellular functions.
source: The non-receptor tyrosine kinase Src is the representative of a family of structure-related kinases initially discovered as a proto-oncogene regulating critical cellular functions (Oppermann et al., 1979).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Src activation mainly occurs downstream of multiple transmembrane receptors, including epidermal growth factor receptor (EGF-R), fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGF-R), and insulin-like growth factor-1 receptor (IGF-1R).
source: Src activation mainly occurs downstream of multiple transmembrane receptors, including epidermal growth factor receptor (EGF-R), fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGF-R), and insulin-like growth factor-1 receptor (IGF-1R).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Src activation.

claim: A dysregulated Src activity has been associated with tumor growth and metastasis, inflammation-mediated carcinogenesis, and therapeutic resistance to traditional antineoplastic drugs.
source: Indeed, a dysregulated Src activity has been associated with tumor growth and metastasis, inflammation-mediated carcinogenesis, and therapeutic resistance to traditional antineoplastic drugs (Caner et al., 2021; Ahn et al., 2018; Cardin et al., 2018; Dosch et al., 2020; Roskoski, 2015; Shao et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: The induction of Src kinase activity can occur following Aryl hydrocarbon Receptor (AhR) activation.
source: The induction of Src kinase activity can also occur following Aryl hydrocarbon Receptor (AhR) activation, whose conformational changes favor the Src-AhR disjunction, allowing the former to phosphorylate its downstream partner IDO1 and thereby promote the generation of an immunoregulatory milieu (Manni et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: AhR conformational changes favor the Src-AhR disjunction, allowing Src to phosphorylate its downstream partner IDO1.
source: The induction of Src kinase activity can also occur following Aryl hydrocarbon Receptor (AhR) activation, whose conformational changes favor the Src-AhR disjunction, allowing the former to phosphorylate its downstream partner IDO1 and thereby promote the generation of an immunoregulatory milieu (Manni et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Src-mediated phosphorylation of IDO1 promotes the generation of an immunoregulatory milieu.
source: The induction of Src kinase activity can also occur following Aryl hydrocarbon Receptor (AhR) activation, whose conformational changes favor the Src-AhR disjunction, allowing the former to phosphorylate its downstream partner IDO1 and thereby promote the generation of an immunoregulatory milieu (Manni et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Src possesses an N-terminal Src homology-4 (SH4) domain, a unique domain, an SH3 domain, an SH2 domain, an SH2-kinase linker domain, and a C-terminal autoregulatory motif.
source: In addition to the kinase domain, Src possesses an N-terminal Src homology-4 (SH4) domain, a unique domain, an SH3 domain, an SH2 domain, an SH2-kinase linker domain, and a C-terminal autoregulatory motif (Roskoski, 2015).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about Src supported by a citation.

claim: The SH2 and SH3 modules serve in protein–protein interactions that are essential for the regulation of kinase activity and signaling function.
source: The SH2 and SH3 modules serve in protein–protein interactions that are essential for the regulation of kinase activity and signaling function.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Src structure-function relationships.

claim: The SH2 domain contains two distinct binding pockets.
source: Specifically, the SH2 domain contains two distinct binding pockets.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about the SH2 domain.

claim: The first pocket of the SH2 domain has a conserved arginine residue that binds a phosphotyrosine (pY) residue presented by the protein substrate.
source: The first one has a conserved arginine residue that binds a phosphotyrosine (pY) residue presented by the protein substrate, whereas the second pocket binds the residue that is three positions C-terminal of pY (pY+3), contributing to the specificity in ligand–protein recognition.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about the SH2 domain.

claim: The second pocket of the SH2 domain binds the residue that is three positions C-terminal of pY (pY+3), contributing to the specificity in ligand–protein recognition.
source: The first one has a conserved arginine residue that binds a phosphotyrosine (pY) residue presented by the protein substrate, whereas the second pocket binds the residue that is three positions C-terminal of pY (pY+3), contributing to the specificity in ligand–protein recognition.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about the SH2 domain.

claim: The autoregulatory function of Src kinase occurs through intramolecular interactions that stabilize the catalytically inactive conformation.
source: The autoregulatory function of the kinase occurs through intramolecular interactions that stabilize the catalytically inactive conformation of Src, in which the SH2 domain binds to a pY located at position +530 of the human sequence.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Src regulation.

claim: In the inactive conformation of Src, the SH2 domain binds to a pY located at position +530 of the human sequence.
source: The autoregulatory function of the kinase occurs through intramolecular interactions that stabilize the catalytically inactive conformation of Src, in which the SH2 domain binds to a pY located at position +530 of the human sequence.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Src regulation.

claim: Binding of ligand proteins to the SH2 domain displaces intramolecular contacts and promotes the catalytic activation of the Src kinase.
source: Accordingly, binding of ligand proteins to the SH2 domain displaces intramolecular contacts and promotes the catalytic activation of the Src kinase, which is characterized by the phosphorylation of a tyrosine residue in the activation loop (Y419 of the human sequence).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Src activation mechanism.

claim: The catalytic activation of Src kinase is characterized by the phosphorylation of a tyrosine residue in the activation loop (Y419 of the human sequence).
source: Accordingly, binding of ligand proteins to the SH2 domain displaces intramolecular contacts and promotes the catalytic activation of the Src kinase, which is characterized by the phosphorylation of a tyrosine residue in the activation loop (Y419 of the human sequence).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Src activation.

claim: Small peptidomimetics destabilize the closed conformation and promote kinase activation through the binding of SH3 and/or SH2 domains.
source: Small peptidomimetics destabilize the closed conformation and thus promote the kinase activation through the binding of SH3 and/or SH2 domains (Moroco et al., 2015; Moroco et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Modulators of Src kinases able to reinforce the intramolecular interactions have proven to allosterically inhibit the enzyme activity.
source: Alternatively, modulators of Src kinases able to reinforce the intramolecular interactions have proven to allosterically inhibit the enzyme activity (Dorman et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Spermidine activates Src kinase with an allosteric mechanism.
source: We found that spermidine (1) activates Src kinase with an allosteric mechanism; (2) binds directly Src kinase at a previously unknown allosteric site; (3) favors the association of IDO1 and Src kinase.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by kinetic data showing non-competitive activation.

claim: Spermidine binds directly Src kinase at a previously unknown allosteric site.
source: We found that spermidine (1) activates Src kinase with an allosteric mechanism; (2) binds directly Src kinase at a previously unknown allosteric site; (3) favors the association of IDO1 and Src kinase.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by docking studies and mutagenesis experiments.

claim: Spermidine favors the association of IDO1 and Src kinase.
source: We found that spermidine (1) activates Src kinase with an allosteric mechanism; (2) binds directly Src kinase at a previously unknown allosteric site; (3) favors the association of IDO1 and Src kinase.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by co-immunoprecipitation and proximity ligation assay data.

claim: Spermidine activated rhSrc with a half-maximal effective concentration (EC50) of 106.4 ± 13.4 nM.
source: Results showed that spermidine activated rhSrc with a half-maximal effective concentration (EC50) of 106.4 ± 13.4 nM (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the ADP-Glo kinase assay shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Spermidine promoted Src phosphorylation in SYF cells with an EC50 of 6.4 ± 0.6 μM.
source: Results showed that the metabolite promoted Src phosphorylation with an EC50 of 6.4 ± 0.6 μM (Figure 1B, C).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figures 1B and 1C.

claim: Spermidine activates Src in MC38 cells endogenously expressing Src.
source: In addition, by measuring the kinase activity in cells endogenously expressing Src (i.e., the murine colon cancer cell line MC38), we confirmed the ability of the polyamine to activate Src (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Spermidine did not activate Src in the absence of either ATP or peptide substrate.
source: Results showed that spermidine did not activate Src in the absence of either ATP or peptide (Figure 1E), while it promoted the production of ADP when the substrate is also present, ruling out any competition for the same site.
evidence: This is supported by kinase assay data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Spermidine promoted the production of ADP when the peptide substrate is present.
source: Results showed that spermidine did not activate Src in the absence of either ATP or peptide (Figure 1E), while it promoted the production of ADP when the substrate is also present, ruling out any competition for the same site.
evidence: This is supported by kinase assay data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: In the presence of fixed amount of spermidine and increasing concentration of the peptide, the maximum rate of Src kinase activity (Vmax) and the affinity (Km) for the substrate increase.
source: In the presence of fixed amount of spermidine and increasing concentration of the peptide, the maximum rate of Src kinase activity (Vmax) and the affinity (Km) for the substrate increase (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by Michaelis-Menten kinetic analysis shown in Figure 1F.

claim: In the presence of different concentration of ATP, spermidine did not affect neither the efficacy nor the affinity of Src kinase.
source: On the contrary, in the presence of different concentration of ATP, spermidine did not affect neither the efficacy nor the affinity of Src kinase (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by kinetic data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The kinetic profile of spermidine is consistent with a non-ATP competition, suggesting that spermidine allosterically activates the kinase activity of Src.
source: Such a kinetic profile is consistent with a non-ATP competition, suggesting that spermidine allosterically activates the kinase activity of Src.
evidence: This is inferred from the kinetic data showing no effect on ATP binding but effects on peptide substrate kinetics.

claim: Spermidine is not able to activate Src Y529F as measured by its phosphorylation.
source: Results demonstrated that the polyamine is not able to activate Src Y529F as measured by its phosphorylation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), suggesting that spermidine per se cannot activate or stabilize the constitutive active form of Src, instead it might promote the conformational changes of the kinase and thus its activation.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Spermidine per se cannot activate or stabilize the constitutive active form of Src.
source: Results demonstrated that the polyamine is not able to activate Src Y529F as measured by its phosphorylation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), suggesting that spermidine per se cannot activate or stabilize the constitutive active form of Src, instead it might promote the conformational changes of the kinase and thus its activation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that spermidine does not activate the constitutively active Y529F mutant.

claim: Spermidine might promote the conformational changes of the kinase and thus its activation.
source: Results demonstrated that the polyamine is not able to activate Src Y529F as measured by its phosphorylation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), suggesting that spermidine per se cannot activate or stabilize the constitutive active form of Src, instead it might promote the conformational changes of the kinase and thus its activation.
evidence: This is speculated based on the inability of spermidine to activate the constitutively active mutant.

claim: In the inactive state, Src assumes a closed conformation with the SH3 domain bound to the SH2-kinase linker and the SH2 domain bound to the tyrosine phosphorylated tail.
source: In the inactive state, Src assumes a closed conformation with the SH3 domain bound to the SH2-kinase linker and the SH2 domain bound to the tyrosine phosphorylated tail (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about Src illustrated in Figure 2A.

claim: A positive electrostatic potential was observed in the region of the pY-binding site (R178 and H204 residues according to sequence numbering of human isoform).
source: A positive electrostatic potential was observed in the region of the pY-binding site (R178 and H204 residues according to sequence numbering of human isoform, Figure 2B), whereas a stretch of surface endowed with a strong negative electrostatic potential was observed on the backside of the pY-binding site as delimited by glutamate residues E150 and E169 (Figure 2B), suggesting the existence of a putative allosteric site.
evidence: This is supported by electrostatic potential calculations shown in Figure 2B.

claim: A stretch of surface endowed with a strong negative electrostatic potential was observed on the backside of the pY-binding site as delimited by glutamate residues E150 and E169.
source: A positive electrostatic potential was observed in the region of the pY-binding site (R178 and H204 residues according to sequence numbering of human isoform, Figure 2B), whereas a stretch of surface endowed with a strong negative electrostatic potential was observed on the backside of the pY-binding site as delimited by glutamate residues E150 and E169 (Figure 2B), suggesting the existence of a putative allosteric site.
evidence: This is supported by electrostatic potential calculations shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The negative electrostatic potential on the backside of the pY-binding site suggests the existence of a putative allosteric site.
source: A positive electrostatic potential was observed in the region of the pY-binding site (R178 and H204 residues according to sequence numbering of human isoform, Figure 2B), whereas a stretch of surface endowed with a strong negative electrostatic potential was observed on the backside of the pY-binding site as delimited by glutamate residues E150 and E169 (Figure 2B), suggesting the existence of a putative allosteric site.
evidence: This is inferred from the electrostatic potential calculations.

claim: The glutamate residues E150 and E169 are conserved in Src protein of human, murine and viral isoforms.
source: Of note, by the alignment of amino acid sequences, we identified that such residues were conserved in Src protein of human, murine and viral isoforms (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), further supporting potential functional role for this allosteric site.
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The conservation of E150 and E169 residues further supports a potential functional role for this allosteric site.
source: Of note, by the alignment of amino acid sequences, we identified that such residues were conserved in Src protein of human, murine and viral isoforms (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), further supporting potential functional role for this allosteric site.
evidence: This is inferred from the sequence conservation data.

claim: According to the top scored docking solution, the first primary amine group of spermidine interacts by an electrostatic enforced hydrogen bond with E150.
source: According to the top scored solution (Supplementary file 1; Figure 2D), the first primary amine group interacts by an electrostatic enforced hydrogen bond with E150, the secondary amine group forms electrostatic enforced hydrogen bond with E150 and the carbonyl group of T250, the other primary amine group makes hydrogen bonds with the side chain of E150 and the carbonyl group of A148 while engaging the aromatic ring of F153 through a specific π-cation interaction (Macchiarulo et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by docking study results shown in Figure 2D and Supplementary file 1.

claim: The secondary amine group of spermidine forms electrostatic enforced hydrogen bond with E150 and the carbonyl group of T250.
source: According to the top scored solution (Supplementary file 1; Figure 2D), the first primary amine group interacts by an electrostatic enforced hydrogen bond with E150, the secondary amine group forms electrostatic enforced hydrogen bond with E150 and the carbonyl group of T250, the other primary amine group makes hydrogen bonds with the side chain of E150 and the carbonyl group of A148 while engaging the aromatic ring of F153 through a specific π-cation interaction (Macchiarulo et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by docking study results shown in Figure 2D and Supplementary file 1.

claim: The other primary amine group of spermidine makes hydrogen bonds with the side chain of E150 and the carbonyl group of A148 while engaging the aromatic ring of F153 through a specific π-cation interaction.
source: According to the top scored solution (Supplementary file 1; Figure 2D), the first primary amine group interacts by an electrostatic enforced hydrogen bond with E150, the secondary amine group forms electrostatic enforced hydrogen bond with E150 and the carbonyl group of T250, the other primary amine group makes hydrogen bonds with the side chain of E150 and the carbonyl group of A148 while engaging the aromatic ring of F153 through a specific π-cation interaction (Macchiarulo et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by docking study results shown in Figure 2D and Supplementary file 1.

claim: The mutation of the glutamate residues E149 and E168 abrogated the kinase activation by spermidine.
source: On evaluating the activation of Src by spermidine, we found that the mutation of the glutamate residues abrogated the kinase activation (Figure 2E, F).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figures 2E and 2F.

claim: The split-luciferase fragment complementation assay confirmed that E149 and E168 are key anchoring points for spermidine binding.
source: The split-luciferase fragment complementation assay confirmed that E149 and E168 are key anchoring points for spermidine binding.
evidence: This is supported by the split-luciferase assay data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: When the endogenous Src is active, the tyrosine residue of the consensus peptide is phosphorylated and interacts with the docking pocket of the SH2 domain, creating a steric hindrance that prevents the reconstitution of a functional luciferase.
source: When the endogenous Src is active, the tyrosine residue of the consensus peptide is phosphorylated and interact with the docking pocket of the SH2 domain. This creates a steric hindrance that prevents the reconstitution of a functional luciferase, resulting in a reduction of bioluminescent signal (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is the mechanism of the split-luciferase reporter assay illustrated in Figure 2G.

claim: The bioluminescence decreased when spermidine is applied only in cells ectopically expressing wild-type Src.
source: Results demonstrated that the bioluminescence decreased when spermidine is applied only in cells ectopically expressing wild-type Src (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is supported by the split-luciferase assay data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: In the absence of spermidine, cells reconstituted with the reporter and the different mutants of Src did not generate statistically different luminescent signal.
source: Of note, in the absence of spermidine, cells – those reconstituted with the reporter and the different mutants of Src – did not generate statistically different luminescent signal (617.7 ± 121 vs 552.2 ± 68.9 vs 501 ± 110, WT Src vs E149A vs E168A, respectively).
evidence: This is supported by the split-luciferase assay data.

claim: The basal activity of the kinase is not affected by the specific amino acid substitution at E149 or E168.
source: This suggests that the basal activity of the kinase is not affected by the specific amino acid substitution.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that baseline luminescence is similar across mutants.

claim: There is a previously unknown allosteric site on the backside of Src SH2 domain as defined by the glutamate residues at positions 150 and 169 of the human sequence.
source: Overall, these data suggested the presence of a previously unknown allosteric site on the backside of Src SH2 domain as defined by the glutamate residues at positions 150 and 169 of the human sequence.
evidence: This is concluded from the combined docking and mutagenesis data.

claim: Spermidine, by means of ionic and hydrogen bond interactions between its protonated amino groups and residues of the shallow anionic site on the SH2 domain, directly associates with and activates Src kinase.
source: Spermidine, by means of ionic and hydrogen bond interactions between its protonated amino groups and residues of the shallow anionic site on the SH2 domain, directly associates with and activates Src kinase.
evidence: This is concluded from the combined docking, mutagenesis, and kinase activity data.

claim: No direct interaction was observed between spermidine and E169 in the docking study.
source: It is worth noting that no direct interaction was observed between spermidine and E169 in the docking study.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the docking study.

claim: E169 may play an indirect role in promoting long-range electrostatic interactions to accomplish the molecular recognition of the cognate ligand into the allosteric site.
source: This may be ascribed to the limit of the scoring function in identifying a binding mode engaging E169 among resulting solutions, or to an indirect role of such residue in promoting long-range electrostatic interactions to accomplish the molecular recognition of the cognate ligand into the allosteric site.
evidence: This is speculated based on the lack of direct interaction in docking but the functional importance shown by mutagenesis.

claim: Only the glutamate residue at position 149 of murine Src is conserved across SH2 domains of Src, Yes, and Fyn, while the glutamate residue at position 168 is replaced by the amino acid glycine.
source: Moreover, the alignment of murine Src, Yes, and Fyn sequences highlighted that only the glutamate residue at position 149 of murine Src is conserved across SH2 domains, while the glutamate residue at position 168 is replaced by the amino acid glycine (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated based on sequence alignment analysis.

claim: The lack of the negative charge at position 168 in related Src kinases may reduce the long-range electrostatic interactions responsible for the molecular recognition of spermidine into the allosteric site.
source: Thus, although we cannot exclude that spermidine can bind the SH2 domain of related Src kinases, we might speculate that the lack of the negative charge at position 168 reduces the long-range electrostatic interactions that we hypothesized to be responsible for the molecular recognition of the ligand into the allosteric site.
evidence: This is speculated based on the sequence differences between Src family kinases.

claim: IDO1 is endowed with non-enzymatic properties aside from metabolizing the amino acid tryptophan.
source: Indeed, aside metabolizing the amino acid tryptophan, IDO1 is endowed with non-enzymatic properties (Mondanelli et al., 2020a; Albini et al., 2017; Pallotta et al., 2011; Orabona et al., 2012; Orecchini et al., 2023; Albini et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: The non-enzymatic properties of IDO1 rely on the presence of two ITIMs (immunoreceptor-tyrosine-based inhibitory motif) that can be phosphorylated in response to immunomodulatory stimuli.
source: The latter relies on the presence of two ITIMs (immunoreceptor-tyrosine-based inhibitory motif) that can be phosphorylated in response to immunomodulatory stimuli, such as TGF(transforming growth factor)-β, L-kynurenine, and spermidine (Mondanelli et al., 2017; Manni et al., 2020; Pallotta et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: IDO1 ITIMs can be phosphorylated in response to immunomodulatory stimuli, such as TGF-β, L-kynurenine, and spermidine.
source: The latter relies on the presence of two ITIMs (immunoreceptor-tyrosine-based inhibitory motif) that can be phosphorylated in response to immunomodulatory stimuli, such as TGF(transforming growth factor)-β, L-kynurenine, and spermidine (Mondanelli et al., 2017; Manni et al., 2020; Pallotta et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: IDO1 phosphorylation increased when Src is co-expressed and activated by spermidine.
source: Results from immunoblot demonstrated that IDO1 phosphorylation increased when Src is co-expressed and activated by spermidine (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: In the presence of a constitutive active Src (i.e., Src Y529F) IDO1 phosphorylation increases regardless of the stimulation with spermidine.
source: In addition, we found that in the presence of a constitutive active Src (i.e., Src Y529F) IDO1 phosphorylation increases regardless of the stimulation with spermidine (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Spermidine can act as an on/off switcher of the kinase, without potentiating the constitutively active protein.
source: This suggests that spermidine can act as an on/off switcher of the kinase, without potentiating the constitutively active protein.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that spermidine does not further activate the constitutively active Y529F mutant.

claim: IDO1 was phosphorylated in a time-dependent manner in the in vitro kinase assay.
source: By detecting phosphotyrosine residues with a specific antibody, we found that IDO1 was phosphorylated in a time-dependent manner (Figure 3B, C).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro kinase assay data shown in Figures 3B and 3C.

claim: In the presence of spermidine, Src quicker phosphorylated IDO1, as demonstrated by the twofold increase of the relative velocity.
source: Moreover, in the presence of spermidine, Src quicker phosphorylated IDO1, as demonstrated by the twofold increase of the relative velocity (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro kinase assay data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: When cells were treated with spermidine for 60 min, IDO1 was found in a complex with Src.
source: Co-immunoprecipitation followed by immunoblot studies demonstrated that when cells were treated with spermidine for 60 min, IDO1 was found in a complex with Src (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Spermidine treatment induced the Src-IDO1 interaction in SYF cells reconstituted with wild-type Src, but not with the E149A or E168A mutant form of the kinase.
source: Accordingly, spermidine treatment induced the Src-IDO1 interaction in SYF cells reconstituted with wild-type Src, but not with the E149A or E168A mutant form of the kinase (Figure 3F, G).
evidence: This is supported by proximity ligation assay data shown in Figures 3F and 3G.

claim: When MC38 cells are exposed to spermidine, the phosphorylation of IDO1 increased.
source: Results demonstrated that when MC38 cells are exposed to spermidine, the phosphorylation of IDO1 increased (Figure 3H) as well as the IDO1/Src interaction (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: When MC38 cells are exposed to spermidine, the IDO1/Src interaction increased.
source: Results demonstrated that when MC38 cells are exposed to spermidine, the phosphorylation of IDO1 increased (Figure 3H) as well as the IDO1/Src interaction (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Spermidine not only accelerates the Src-mediated phosphorylation of IDO1, but also promotes the formation of Src–IDO1 complex.
source: As a whole, these results suggested that spermidine not only accelerates the Src-mediated phosphorylation of IDO1, but also promotes the formation of Src–IDO1 complex.
evidence: This is concluded from the combined kinase assay, co-immunoprecipitation, and proximity ligation assay data.

claim: Src is involved in several signaling pathways regulating key cellular processes as well as immune responses.
source: The non-receptor tyrosine kinase Src is the representative of a family of structure-related enzymes involved in several signaling pathways regulating key cellular processes as well as immune responses (Caner et al., 2021; Liu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Much relevant literature correlates dysregulated Src kinase activity with cancer.
source: Much relevant literature correlates dysregulated Src kinase activity with cancer and thus extensive efforts have been made to develop small molecules kinase inhibitors.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the field.

claim: Currently, approved kinase inhibitors are compounds that reversibly bind the catalytic site and thus compete with the ligand (i.e., ATP).
source: Currently, approved kinase inhibitors are compounds that reversibly bind the catalytic site and thus compete with the ligand (i.e., ATP) (Roskoski, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: As the ATP-binding cleft is structurally well conserved among kinases, ATP-competitive inhibitors are poorly selective.
source: As the ATP-binding cleft is structurally well conserved among kinases, these inhibitors are poorly selective.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural conservation of the ATP-binding site.

claim: Chronic usage of ATP-competitive kinase inhibitors is frequently associated with acquired drug resistance that ultimately limits patients' compliance and the therapeutic success.
source: Moreover, their chronic usage is frequently associated with acquired drug resistance that ultimately limits patients' compliance and the therapeutic success.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about kinase inhibitor therapy.

claim: The FDA-approved Dasatinib and Bosutinib inhibit more than 30 kinases, and thus are not suitable for probing Src-dependent pharmacology.
source: For instance, the FDA-approved Dasatinib and Bosutinib inhibit more than 30 kinases, and thus are not suitable for probing Src-dependent pharmacology (Ozanne et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Saracatinib is another example of small molecule that interacts with the ATP-binding pocket.
source: Saracatinib is another example of small molecule that interacts with the ATP-binding pocket.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about Saracatinib.

claim: Although Saracatinib is more selective than Dasatinib, it potently inhibits EGF-R as well.
source: Although more selective than Dasatinib, it potently inhibits EGF-R as well (Formisano et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The promiscuity of molecules interacting with the ATP pocket has moved the interest toward the development of alternative strategies for more effective and less-toxic inhibitors.
source: However, the promiscuity of molecules interacting with the ATP pocket has moved the interest toward the development of alternative strategies for more effective and less-toxic inhibitors.
evidence: This is stated as a rationale for developing alternative approaches.

claim: Src protein has structural plasticity, that is, the capability to adopt distinct conformations due to intrinsic dynamic properties.
source: The peculiarity of the Src protein, as well as of other tyrosine kinases, is its structural plasticity, that is, the capability to adopt distinct conformations due to intrinsic dynamic properties (Engen et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The activation state of Src protein kinase is dictated by dynamic intramolecular interactions between the SH3, SH2, and kinase domains.
source: The activation state of this protein kinase is indeed dictated by dynamic intramolecular interactions between the SH3, SH2, and kinase domains.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Src regulation.

claim: The SH2 domain plays a key role in both autoregulating Src kinase activity and in recruiting the protein ligand.
source: The SH2 domain plays a key role in both autoregulating Src kinase activity and in recruiting the protein ligand.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the SH2 domain function.

claim: The tyrosine residue at position +530, when phosphorylated, interacts with the SH2 domain and stabilizes a restrained catalytically inactive conformation of Src.
source: Specifically, the tyrosine residue at position +530, when phosphorylated, interacts with the SH2 domain and stabilizes a restrained catalytically inactive conformation of Src (Shah et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The activating event of Src is mostly driven by a dynamic breakage and formation of electrostatic interactions that involve salt bridges and hydrogen bonds.
source: This activating event is mostly driven by a dynamic breakage and formation of electrostatic interactions that involve salt bridges and hydrogen bonds.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Src activation mechanism.

claim: Allosteric modulation has been proposed as pharmacological approach to target the activity of Src kinase.
source: Guided by the dynamic nature of the kinase, allosteric modulation has been proposed as pharmacological approach to target the activity of Src kinase.
evidence: This is stated as an established approach in the field.

claim: Allosteric molecules do not possess intrinsic efficacy, but instead modulate – either positively or negatively – the activity of orthosteric agonists.
source: Allosteric molecules do not possess intrinsic efficacy, but instead modulate – either positively or negatively – the activity of orthosteric agonists.
evidence: This is established knowledge about allosteric modulators.

claim: Allosteric hotspots, being less conserved among kinases, ensure greater drug selectivity.
source: Moreover, being less conserved among kinases, the allosteric hotspots ensure greater drug selectivity.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural diversity of allosteric sites compared to ATP-binding sites.

claim: Targetable allosteric pockets have been identified for few kinases as reported for Hck, Lyn, Aurora A kinase, and Bcr-Abl.
source: Targetable allosteric pockets have been identified for few kinases as reported for Hck, Lyn, Aurora A kinase, and Bcr-Abl (Dorman et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2010; Saporito et al., 2012; Panicker et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Modulators of the SH2 and SH3 domains have been developed as chemical tools modifying the conformation and thus both the enzymatic and non-enzymatic functions of Src.
source: In addition, modulators of the SH2 and SH3 domains – either peptidomimetics or small molecules – have been developed as chemical tools modifying the conformation and thus both the enzymatic and non-enzymatic functions of Src, the latter including protein–protein interactions and intracellular localization (Moroco et al., 2015; Moroco et al., 2014; Saporito et al., 2012; Leonard et al., 2014; Fischer et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: The non-enzymatic functions of Src include protein–protein interactions and intracellular localization.
source: In addition, modulators of the SH2 and SH3 domains – either peptidomimetics or small molecules – have been developed as chemical tools modifying the conformation and thus both the enzymatic and non-enzymatic functions of Src, the latter including protein–protein interactions and intracellular localization (Moroco et al., 2015; Moroco et al., 2014; Saporito et al., 2012; Leonard et al., 2014; Fischer et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about Src functions.

claim: Metabolites are chemicals that do not merely take place in the metabolic reactions, but are also involved in inter- and intracellular communications, energy production, macromolecule synthesis, post-translational modifications, and cell survival.
source: Metabolites are chemicals that do not merely take place in the metabolic reactions, but are also involved in inter- and intracellular communications, energy production, macromolecule synthesis, post-translational modifications, and cell survival (Gargaro et al., 2022; Makowski et al., 2020; Icard et al., 2019; Diskin et al., 2021; Mondanelli and Volpi, 2021; Mondanelli and Volpi, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: The enzymes responsible for metabolite production are considered central regulators of the function of cells, including immune cells.
source: In accordance, the enzymes responsible for their production are considered central regulators of the function of cells, including immune cells (Giovanelli et al., 2019; Grohmann et al., 2017; Sun et al., 2022; Mandarano et al., 2020; Bonometti et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: IDO1 is the prototype of metabolic enzymes acting at the forefront of immune responses.
source: IDO1 is the prototype of such metabolic enzymes acting at the forefront of immune responses.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about IDO1.

claim: Thanks to its catalytic activity as well as non-enzymatic function (relying on the phosphorylation of its ITIMs), IDO1 is a tiebreaker of tolerance and immunity.
source: Thanks to its catalytic activity as well as non-enzymatic function (relying on the phosphorylation of its ITIMs), IDO1 is a tiebreaker of tolerance and immunity (Grohmann et al., 2017; Mondanelli et al., 2019; Iacono et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: An endogenous metabolite, when present at specific concentrations, can directly activate Src kinase without requiring a membrane receptor.
source: Our data provided evidence that an endogenous metabolite, when present at specific concentrations, can directly activate Src kinase without requiring a membrane receptor.
evidence: This is concluded from the experimental data showing direct activation of recombinant Src by spermidine.

claim: By acting on the backside of the SH2 domain, spermidine not only modulates the catalytic activity, but also affects the scaffold function of Src in organizing transducing signaling complexes.
source: By acting on the backside of the SH2 domain, that is the domain responsible for the substrate binding, spermidine not only modulates the catalytic activity, but also affects the scaffold function of Src in organizing transducing signaling complexes – as those with IDO1 – which could be relevant in many diseases.
evidence: This is concluded from the combined data showing both kinase activation and enhanced protein-protein interactions.

claim: The results provide the proof of principle for the development of molecules that can modulate the kinase activity and the non-enzymatic functions of Src and IDO1 at once.
source: Thus, from a therapeutic perspective, our results provide the proof of principle for the development of molecules that can modulate the kinase activity and the non-enzymatic functions of Src and IDO1 at once.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential therapeutic applications based on the findings.

claim: SYF cells are fibroblasts null for Src family kinases, Src, Yes, and Fyn.
source: SYF cells that is fibroblast null for Src family kinases, Src, Yes, and Fyn (Klinghoffer et al., 1999) were stably transfected with vector encoding for murine Src kinase and then treated with increasing concentration of spermidine.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the SYF cell line supported by a citation.

claim: Lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) is a stimulus known to activate Src kinase downstream the LPA2 receptor in SYF cells.
source: To validate the functional equivalence of Src mutants, cells were exposed to lysophosphatidic acid (LPA), a stimulus known to activate Src kinase downstream the LPA2 receptor in SYF cells (Lai et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Src activity is induced by LPA as measured by the phosphorylation of the Y418, independently of the mutation at the putative allosteric site.
source: Results indicated that Src activity is induced by LPA as measured by the phosphorylation of the Y418, independently of the mutation at the putative allosteric site (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The SH2 domain of the viral Src kinase shares a high sequence identity (97%) with the relative SH2 domains of human and murine Src tyrosine kinase.
source: It should be mentioned that the SH2 domain of the viral Src kinase shares a high sequence identity (97%) with the relative SH2 domains of human and murine Src tyrosine kinase (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: It is possible to use the NMR structure of the viral isoform with very good approximation to infer about the electrostatic potential map of human SH2 domain and to investigate the putative binding site of spermidine.
source: Hence, it is possible to use the NMR structure of the viral isoform with very good approximation to infer about the electrostatic potential map of human SH2 domain and to investigate the putative binding site of spermidine.
evidence: This is inferred from the high sequence identity between viral and human Src SH2 domains.
